I visited the centre with my wife after taking an advance appointment for 5:30 PM. We were told to reach by 5:15 PM, which we did. However, even after arriving on time, we were made to wait until 6:30 PM. Each time we asked, we were given different excuses like two patients are waiting or one more patient is ahead.
The reception staff were extremely unprofessional. They neither informed us properly nor communicated politely. They only responded when we repeatedly went to ask, and even then, the response was just please wait, you will be called without any clarity.
Also, the contact number provided by SRDC gives different information, and when we questioned the staff at the centre, they blamed the call center, saying the call center gave wrong details. If the call center belongs to SRDC, then why is incorrect information being shared with patients?
Overall, very poor coordination, lack of professionalism, and disrespect for patients’ time. Would like to suggest go visit any other diagnostic centre but not here..

The virus primarily targets the central nervous system (CNS), causing a condition known as rabies encephalitis, which leads to brain inflammation, coma, and death.

Once a person becomes symptomatic, recovery is extremely rare. However, rabies is 100% preventable through timely vaccination and proper wound care. That is why awareness and prompt action are critical.

Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are a group of disorders that affect the heart and blood vessels. They include conditions such as coronary artery disease, stroke, heart failure, arrhythmias, peripheral artery disease, and congenital heart defects. These diseases interfere with the normal functioning of the heart, impacting how efficiently it pumps blood to the rest of the body. Over time, if left unmanaged, CVD can lead to severe disability or sudden death.

The impact of CVD on health is not limited to just heart function. It affects physical endurance, brain function, kidney health, and even mental well-being. Blood flow carries oxygen and nutrients to every organ, so impaired circulation has widespread consequences.
